components.name: Button
components.summary: A button, or a link that looks like one when it has an `href`.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.summary: Buttons joined together. It needs a label, because a group is a landmark for assistive technology.

components.name: Toggle
components.summary: A two-state button. It is a checkbox underneath, so it posts with its form, keeps its state with no script and has the keyboard of a checkbox.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.summary: A group of toggles that post as one field.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.summary: A button and the menu it opens.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.summary: A region and the menu its right click opens.

components.name: Menubar
components.summary: A bar of menus.

components.name: Field
components.summary: A control with its label, help and error, tied together with `for`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`.

components.name: Input
components.summary: A single-line input.

components.name: InputGroup
components.summary: An input with something fixed before or after it.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A multi-line input. It grows with its text where the browser can.

components.name: NativeSelect
components.summary: The browser's `<select>`.

components.name: Select
components.summary: One choice from a small, fixed list, in a styled listbox.

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: One choice, found by typing. The options are in the page, or searched on the server.

components.name: MultiSelect
components.summary: Many choices, shown as chips with a 4 px corner.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A checkbox.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: An on and off switch: a checkbox with the `switch` role.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.summary: One choice out of several, shown: a `fieldset` of native radios, whose keyboard is the browser's.

components.name: PhoneInput
components.summary: A phone number input with a country picker.

components.name: Upload
components.summary: A file field with a drop area, a list of the files and, in a form of its own, progress.

components.name: Forms
components.summary: Draws a `Form`: a `<form>` that posts with or without the runtime.

components.name: InputOtp
components.summary: A field for a one-time code, such as the six digits a text message carries.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.summary: A colour field. The colour is the browser's own `<input type="color">`, which posts `#rrggbb` and has the platform's picker, its keys and its screen reader support. With a script, a hex field and a row of swatches sit beside it and move in step with it; without one, the colour field alone is drawn, and it posts all the same.

components.name: Questionnaire
components.summary: A form that asks one question at a time. It is server-driven and needs no script: each press of a button posts the page to `action` with the answers so far kept in hidden fields, the posted `_step` (the question counted from 0) and `_move` (see `QuestionnaireMove`), and the server draws the question to show next. The checks are the app's, as for any form; the browser's own check of a required answer runs before Next.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.summary: Avatars side by side, each overlapping the one before, with a `+N` tile for the people left out when there are more than `max`.

components.name: Trace
components.summary: The steps of something that happened, or is happening, down a line: what an agent did, how an import went, where a deploy is. Each step has a mark for its state, which is spoken too, a title, a line of description and detail that opens by itself.

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A calendar: one or more months, with the days that can be chosen.

components.name: DatePicker
components.summary: A date field with a calendar.

components.name: DateRangePicker
components.summary: A range of days from two dates: one button, and a popover with presets beside a calendar of two months.

components.name: TimePicker
components.summary: A time of day: hours and minutes, and seconds if asked.

components.name: DateTimePicker
components.summary: A date and a time of day together: a date box with its calendar and a time box with its list, side by side in one control that posts one value.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface for related content.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A short label beside something.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A picture of a person: an image, or a neutral icon when there is none. There is no way to put initials in it.

components.name: Item
components.summary: A row with a title, a description, and things at either end.

components.name: Heading and Text
components.summary: A heading. The level is the document's, the look follows it.

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: A key on the keyboard.

components.name: Attachment
components.summary: A file shown as a small tile.

components.name: Markdown
components.summary: Text written in Markdown, drawn as HTML that cannot hold anything the text did not say.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: Code, drawn with its colours in the markup.

components.name: Message and Bubble
components.summary: A message in a conversation: who, when, and bubbles.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: Events on a rail.

components.name: ActivityFeed
components.summary: What people did lately, newest first.

components.name: FactCard and FactGrid
components.summary: One fact about something: a small label, a value and the details under it.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message inside the page.

components.name: Toast
components.summary: A message that goes by itself.

components.name: Empty
components.summary: What a list shows when it has nothing in it.

components.name: EmptyState
components.summary: What a list, a table or a region shows when it has nothing in it, with the action each case needs. Built on the same markup as the error states.

components.name: ErrorPage
components.summary: A whole page for an error status: the headline, the explanation, what to do next and a reference for support.

components.name: Forbidden
components.summary: "You don't have access to this": the state for a place the user may not see, for a card, a tab, a region or a table row. It never says whether the thing exists.

components.name: NotFound
components.summary: "We can't find that": the state for a record, a card or a region that isn't there.

components.name: SignInRequired
components.summary: The state for a card, tab or region that needs a signed-in user: a button to the sign-in page that brings the user back to where they were.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: How far along something is: the browser's `<progress>`.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A placeholder while content loads.

components.name: Spinner
components.summary: A sign that something is happening, named for assistive technology.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal dialog: the browser's `<dialog>`, which brings the focus trap, Esc, focus return and the inert page behind it.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.summary: A dialog that must be answered: `alertdialog`, no close button, and a click outside doesn't dismiss it. Esc still cancels, as APG asks.

components.name: Sheet
components.summary: A dialog that slides in from an edge.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A dialog that rises from the bottom, for phones.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A popup with a click-outside and Esc dismissal, from the browser's `popover`, opened by a button.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short description on hover and on focus, with the `tooltip` role.

components.name: HoverCard
components.summary: A popup on hover or focus with more about a link. Sighted mouse users get it; the same content must be reachable another way.

components.name: Stack, Row, Grid and Container
components.summary: Items one above the other.

components.name: SplitPane
components.summary: Panes with separators between them.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: Sections that open and close: `<details>`, whose keyboard is the browser's. With `exclusive`, one open at a time through `name`.

components.name: Collapsible
components.summary: One section that opens and closes.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A scrolling region with thin scrollbars, reachable by keyboard.

components.name: Separator
components.summary: A line between things.

components.name: AspectRatio
components.summary: Content held to a shape. The ratios are a closed set because the content security policy allows no `style` attribute.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: Slides that scroll and snap.

components.name: Direction
components.summary: Sets the reading direction of what's inside.

components.name: App shell
components.summary: The app's one shell definition. Register it as a provider so `AppShell` can find it.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: A list of tabs and their panels.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.summary: The links of a site, with panels of more links.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: Where this page sits: a list of links, ending in the current page.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Links between the pages of a list.

components.name: Command
components.summary: A command palette: a modal dialog with a search box and a list of groups of items, opened by `Ctrl` or `Cmd` and `K`.

components.name: Stepper
components.summary: The steps of a task, in order.

components.name: Wizard
components.summary: A form in steps.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A slider, single or a range.

components.name: TreeView
components.summary: A tree.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A toolbar.

components.name: Table
components.summary: A table of data. The wrapper scrolls on narrow screens, and a keyboard can reach it to scroll it: it is a tab stop. Named with `Table::label`, it is also a region a screen reader lists (two regions of one page need two names).

components.name: DataTable
components.summary: A table with search, filters, sort links, selection and pagination, as one region.

components.name: LazyList
components.summary: A list that loads as it is read, in pages, by cursor. See the module's docs.

components.name: Stat and Bars
components.summary: One figure and what it is: a tile for a dashboard.

components.name: Sortable
components.summary: Lists whose items move, within a list and between lists.

components.name: SortableGrid
components.summary: Tiles in a grid that people put in their own order and take away: the tiles of a dashboard, of a home-screen widget, of a launcher.

components.name: Line chart
components.summary: Change over time: lines on a shared axis, with gaps, targets, events and bands.

components.name: Area chart
components.summary: A line with a wash under it. Stacked, the parts of a total over time.

components.name: Bar chart
components.summary: Bars from one baseline to compare amounts: grouped, stacked, negative, vertical or horizontal.

components.name: Donut chart
components.summary: One whole split into a few parts, with the total in the middle. A pie has no hole.

components.name: Sparkline
components.summary: A small line with no axes, beside a figure: the shape of a series at a glance.

components.name: Funnel
components.summary: How many reach each stage of an ordered process, and what share of the first and of the stage before.

components.name: Ring
components.summary: One value on a ring: a score out of 100, steps toward a goal, with the value in the middle.

components.name: Rings
components.summary: Two to six values on rings inside each other, each against its own goal.

components.name: Gauge
components.summary: One value on an open arc, 270 degrees or any sweep, on a scale that may start above zero.

components.name: Day clock
components.summary: A day round a clock face: a wedge for each hour, its length the value, its colour a category, with moments marked.

components.name: Meter
components.summary: One bar split into segments that add up to the whole, with the share inside the wide ones and a legend of values.

components.name: Mini columns
components.summary: Small multiples: one column per item, each split into the same parts and drawn to 100%.

components.name: Colour strip
components.summary: A row of equal cells, each in the colour of its category or of the band its reading falls in.

components.name: Range scale
components.summary: One value on a scale between two ends, with a marker and a track that can be a gradient.

components.name: Trend
components.summary: Which way something moved and by how much: an arrow, a signed change and a colour for what it means.

components.name: Calendar heat map
components.summary: A day per cell in weeks, shaded in five steps: how consistent a habit is over months. A day with no data is hollow, not zero.

components.name: Matrix heat map
components.summary: Every measure against every other, such as a correlation matrix: a tone for the sign, depth for the strength, neutral for chance and blank for untested.

components.name: Relation list
components.summary: Pairs of measures ranked by how strongly they move together: the signed value, a bar from the centre by sign and a note on each row.

components.name: Scatter chart
components.summary: A translucent point for each pair of values, in one series or several: a cloud of beats, steps against resting heart rate. Axes can be hidden and both can share a range.

components.name: Chart pictures
components.summary: A chart drawn as a PNG on the server, for a home-screen widget, an email or an Open Graph card.

components.name: Info tip
components.summary: A small "?" or (i) chip that opens a note about the thing beside it: how to read a chart, what a score is made of.

components.name: Chart skeleton
components.summary: A loading placeholder shaped like the chart that is coming: a ring, a gauge, a line, bars, a calendar, a matrix or a meter.

components.name: Breathing guide
components.summary: A paced 4-7-8 breathing circle that runs from CSS alone and holds still when the reader asks for less motion.

components.name: Dock
components.summary: A floating row of icon links pinned to the bottom of the page: the main places of an app, with the current one lit.

components.name: Day pager
components.summary: The day before, the day shown and the day after, with the day's scores and a calendar behind the date.

components.name: Copy field
components.summary: A value to take elsewhere, such as an invite link or a key, in a read-only field with a Copy button.

components.name: Auth layout
components.summary: The page of one form a guest fills in, such as signing in or up, with the app's own panel beside it.

components.name: Conversation
components.summary: The messages of a conversation with an assistant, oldest first, loading earlier ones as the reader scrolls up and merging an answer as it is written.

components.name: ChatMessage
components.summary: One message of a conversation, as an item of its `Conversation`.

components.name: PromptInput
components.summary: Where the reader writes to the assistant: a form that posts `message` (and the page's signed context, when there is one) to the composer's route. With no script it is a plain form.

components.name: ToolCallCard and Reasoning
components.summary: A tool the assistant called, with whether it ran and its arguments folded, and what the assistant thought before it answered.

components.name: ApprovalCard
components.summary: A tool call waiting for the reader's answer, drawn by the page in a place of its own, never inside the conversation or a component the model chose: the tool's label, the arguments the model chose as text, and Approve and Reject (with a reason) as forms.

components.name: SurfaceFrame
components.summary: Where a component the model chose is drawn, as an item of the conversation. See the module's docs for what is taken out of what it drew.

components.name: Suggestions
components.summary: Messages the reader can send with one press: each a button of one form that posts it as the message, so they work with no script. The words are the app's.

components.name: Sources and Citation
components.summary: The links an answer drew on, with the host of each that leaves the site, and numbered references to them.

components.name: ThreadList
components.summary: A reader's conversations, newest first, each a link to its page; the open one is marked as the current page.

components.name: Foundations
components.summary: A control's size.

components.name: Themes
components.summary: A theme: an id, a name and a `ThemeSpec`. The built-in ones are associated constants; `Theme::custom` makes your own.

components.name: App styles
components.summary: A stylesheet of the app's own, compiled in with `include_bytes!` and served by the toolkit at `/_navree/ui/app/{name}-{hash}.css` as `immutable`. See the module.

components.name: Theme builder
components.summary: The builder: the form, the preview, the contrast report and the export.

components.name: Icons
components.summary: An icon: its SVG shapes and the box they are drawn in. Compile-time data, so no icon comes from a request.

components.name: Flags
components.summary: A flag, drawn inline from the code of a country, a region or a body.

components.name: Commands
components.summary: One browser-side command.

components.name: Regions
components.summary: A named part of a page that updates by itself: fetched after paint, polled, or refetched when an op invalidates it. Its answer morphs in.

components.name: Errors and states
components.summary: The settings of the error pages `UiModule` draws.

components.name: Reports
components.summary: A report's window and periods.

components.name: Picture
components.summary: A responsive image: the sizes it comes in (`srcset` and `sizes`), AVIF and WebP for the browsers that read them with the original as the fallback (`<picture>`), its width and height so the page keeps its room while it loads, and lazy loading below the fold.

components.name: SitePage
components.summary: A whole public page: a link that skips to the content, then the header, the `<main>` landmark with the page's sections, and the footer. The skip link is the first thing a keyboard reaches and shows itself when it has focus.

components.name: SiteHeader
components.summary: The header of a public site: the brand on the left, the main links in the middle and the calls to action on the right, held at the top as the page scrolls. Below 64 rem the links and actions fold into a menu behind one button: a `<details>`, so it opens and closes with no script, by keyboard and by touch, and says whether it is open.

components.name: Hero
components.summary: The top of a page: a small line, the headline (the page's `h1`), a lead, the calls to action, a row of short notes, and a picture beside them or under them: a screenshot in a `BrowserFrame`, a `PhoneFrame`, a chart, any node.

components.name: Section
components.summary: A part of a page: its heading, its content, in the page's width, with the space above and below that every section shares. Its `id` is what a link to it names (`/#pricing`), and its heading's title names the section for assistive technology.

components.name: LogoCloud
components.summary: A row of the names or marks of those who use the product.

components.name: FeatureGrid
components.summary: Features side by side in cards: two, three or four columns on a wide screen, one on a phone. A `wide` feature with a picture makes it a bento grid.

components.name: FeatureRows
components.summary: Features told one after another, each beside its picture, the picture on the right, then the left, in turn. On a phone each picture is under its words.

components.name: StatBand
components.summary: A band of a few large numbers, each with what it counts.

components.name: Device frames
components.summary: A screenshot or a live part of the product in a browser window or a phone, light or dark.

components.name: Testimonials
components.summary: Testimonials in columns that fill from the top, as many as the width allows.

components.name: Pricing
components.summary: Plans side by side, with a switch between monthly and yearly prices when a plan has both. The switch is a pair of radio buttons and the stylesheet shows the prices of the one chosen, so it works with no script, by keyboard (the arrow keys move between the two) and by touch, and the server can draw either period first.

components.name: Faq
components.summary: Questions and their answers. Each question is a heading (`h3`) in a `<details>`, so it opens with no script and the browser gives it its keyboard and its open or closed state; `exclusive` keeps one open at a time.

components.name: CtaBand
components.summary: A band near the end of a page that asks the reader to act: a title (`h2`), a line and the buttons, centred over soft light from the accent.

components.name: Newsletter
components.summary: A band with a form: a title (`h2`), a line, the form and a small note under it. The form is a `FormView`, so its fields, its checks on the server, its errors and its CSRF token are a form's like any other, and it posts with no script.

components.name: LegalPage
components.summary: A long page of rules: a privacy policy, terms of service, a refund policy. Its title (`h1`), a short introduction and when it last changed, then its parts, with a list of them that links to each: beside the text and held in view on a wide screen, above it on a phone. Lines are kept to a length that reads well.

components.name: SiteFooter
components.summary: The foot of every page: the brand and a line about the site, columns of links, its accounts elsewhere, the small print, and a `ThemeToggle`.

components.name: Build anything
components.summary: A table with search, filters, sort links, selection and pagination, as one region.

examples.code:
use navree::ui::charts::{ColorScale, Gradient, Ink, Motion};
let quality = |value: u32, label: &str, slot: u8, step: u32| {
    Progress::new(value, 100, label.to_owned())
        .ink(Ink::slot(slot))
        .height(8)
        .show_value()
        .motion(Motion::new().delay(300 + step * 100))
};
Stack::gap(4).children((
    Progress::new(402, 480, "Sleep, 6 h 42 min against a goal of 7 h")
        .fill(
            Gradient::horizontal()
                .stop(0.0, Ink::slot(7))
                .stop_with_opacity(1.0, Ink::slot(7), 0.6),
        )
        .goal(420)
        .height(12)
        .motion(Motion::new().delay(200)),
    Progress::new(68, 100, "Recovery 68%, fair")
        .colors(
            ColorScale::new(Ink::tone(Tone::Danger))
                .from(50, Ink::tone(Tone::Warning))
                .from(75, Ink::tone(Tone::Success)),
        )
        .glow()
        .height(8)
        .show_value(),
    quality(91, "Efficiency", 7, 0),
    quality(74, "Depth", 1, 1),
    quality(83, "Continuity", 3, 2),
))

examples.title: Steps between named levels
examples.code:
let start = NaiveDate::from_ymd_opt(2026, 11, 11)
    .and_then(|day| day.and_hms_opt(23, 10, 0))
    .unwrap_or_default();
// Each stage and how long it lasted, in minutes: 0 deep, 1 light, 2 REM, 3 awake.
let night: [(u32, i64); 16] = [
    (1, 20),
    (0, 45),
    (1, 30),
    (2, 15),
    (1, 25),
    (0, 35),
    (1, 40),
    (2, 25),
    (3, 5),
    (1, 35),
    (0, 20),
    (1, 30),
    (2, 35),
    (1, 25),
    (2, 30),
    (3, 10),
];
// A point where each stage starts, and one at waking so the last stage holds.
let mut at = start;
let mut times = Vec::new();
for (_, minutes) in night {
    times.push(at);
    at += Duration::minutes(minutes);
}
times.push(at);
let stages: Vec<u32> = night.iter().map(|(stage, _)| *stage).chain([3]).collect();
let lasted: Vec<String> = night
    .iter()
    .map(|(_, minutes)| format!("{minutes} min"))
    .chain([String::new()])
    .collect();
let stage = |slot: u8| Ink::slot(slot);
Chart::area("Sleep stages")
    .id("area-chart-steps")
    .description("Simran Kaur, night of 11 November")
    .locale("en-IN")
    .height(160)
    .times(times)
    .series(
        Series::new("Stage", stages)
            .ink(Ink::slot(7))
            .fill(
                Gradient::vertical()
                    .stop_with_opacity(0.0, stage(4), 0.3)
                    .stop_with_opacity(0.33, stage(5), 0.35)
                    .stop_with_opacity(0.66, stage(1), 0.35)
                    .stop_with_opacity(1.0, stage(7), 0.45)
                    .across_plot(),
            )
            .colors(
                ColorScale::new(stage(7))
                    .label("Deep")
                    .from(1, stage(1))
                    .label("Light")
                    .from(2, stage(5))
                    .label("REM")
                    .from(3, stage(4))
                    .label("Awake"),
            ),
    )
    .curve(Curve::Step)
    .y_categories(["Deep", "Light", "REM", "Awake"])
    .dots(Dots::None)
    .grid(Gridlines::none())
    .x_ticks(Ticks::most(5).keep_ends())
    .reference(Reference::level(0).ink(stage(7)))
    .reference(Reference::level(1).ink(stage(1)))
    .reference(Reference::level(2).ink(stage(5)))
    .reference(Reference::level(3).ink(stage(4)))
    .detail("Lasted", lasted)
    .tooltip(TooltipStyle::big())

/// An order, as the table shows it. Each column says what a reader can do with
/// it; the server runs the search, the filters, the sort and the pages.
#[derive(Clone, TableRow)]
#[table(
    cursor,
    capped = 10000,
    sort = "-placed_on",
    per = 25,
    per_pages(10, 25, 50, 100)
)]
pub struct OrderRow {
    #[col(skip)]
    pub id: i64,
    #[col(sortable, search, sticky, label = "Order", role = title)]
    pub number: String,
    #[col(search, hidden, role = subtitle)]
    pub customer: String,
    #[col(search, hidden)]
    pub email: String,
    // A relation's choices come from the page: each status with how many hold it.

    #[col(skip)]
    pub placed_at: i64,
}

/// The orders table: one definition drives the query, the filters with their
/// counts, the drawing and the live refresh.
pub fn orders_table<'a>(
    query: &'a TableQuery<OrderRow>,
    page: &'a TablePage<OrderRow>,
    counts: &[(Status, u64)],
    today: NaiveDate,
) -> DataTable<'a, OrderRow> {
    let statuses = counts
        .iter()
        .map(|(status, n)| FilterOption::new(status.key(), status.label()).count(*n))
        .collect();
    DataTable::new("orders", query, page)
        .caption("Orders")
        .options("status", statuses)
        .cell("number", order_cell)
        .cell("status", |row| status_badge(&row.status))
        .cell("fulfilment", |row| fulfilment_badge(&row.fulfilment))
        .cell("payment", |row| payment_badge(&row.payment))
        .cell("total", total_cell)
        .cell("state", place_cell)
        .cell("placed_on", move |row| {
            Text::new(when(row.placed_at, today)).inline()
        })
        // A tap on a row opens the order where the reader is, as its number does.
        .row_opens(|row| format!("/orders/{}/peek", row.id))
        .filter_bar()
        .sticky_header()
        .live_on(crate::live::stream().on("orders"))
        .empty(
            Empty::new("No order matches")
                .icon(icons::SEARCH_X)
                .description(
                    "Clear a filter, or search for an order number, a name or an address.",
                ),
        )
}
